rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Security architecture terms for trust, planes, layers, and boundaries.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: partial deck includes unresolved card definitions; zero whole-container credit under this slice’s conservative boundary.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Five-card grouping of control/data planes, segmentation, layers and perimeter terminology. Opening and flipping these cards does not repair the held Perimeter Security definition or prove an architecture decision.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Zero Trust, serverless, availability, and storage resilience acronyms.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: partial deck includes unresolved card definitions; zero whole-container credit under this slice’s conservative boundary.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Four-card grouping of FaaS, HA, RAID and ZTA. This is a mixed vocabulary collection, not evidence of Zero Trust architecture, achieved availability or recoverability; ZTA teaching remains held.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Cloud responsibility and deployment terms for architecture decisions.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: partial deck includes unresolved card definitions; zero whole-container credit under this slice’s conservative boundary.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Five-card grouping of responsibility and deployment vocabulary. Public Cloud and Hybrid Cloud remain held; successful navigation does not establish a complete deployment-model distinction or a suitable architecture.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Data-state and privacy protection terms for architecture design.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the actual privacy-protection collection states tokens have no useful value outside a vault and anonymization makes people impossible to re-identify. Those unconditional outcomes are unsupported by its own introductory contents; useful authorized tokens and auxiliary-data linkage are counterexamples. The other five state/masking/pseudonymization cards do not repair these two delivered claims. This is an independent whole-container content judgment; existing child holds remain separate and unchanged.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Seven-card grouping of data states and privacy protections. Tokenization and Anonymization retain their exact holds; recall of labels does not establish token uselessness outside a vault or irreversible anonymization.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Availability and recovery architecture terms for keeping services running.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the availability/recovery promise is supported in part, but the geographic-dispersal body claims regions prevent one local disaster taking down the whole service without independent dependencies, usable capacity, data and traffic failover. A shared identity/DNS/control dependency defeats that guarantee. RAID and hot/warm/cold labels teach vocabulary, not a tested service recovery. This whole-container gap is visible in its own delivered content, not inferred solely from a held-child flag.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Ten-card grouping of fault tolerance, RAID, sites, dispersal and load balancing. The held geographic-dispersal guarantee remains; a collection and self-ratings are not a failover or recovery test.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Incident response and forensic handling terms used in security operations.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: every child was inspected but one child remains held; zero whole-container credit.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Seven-card grouping of response and evidence-handling terms. The combined Playbook/Runbook explanation still lacks its component relationship; card reveal does not execute response or validate evidence handling.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Operational terms for logs, flow data, alerting, and evidence integrity.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: every child was inspected but one child remains held; zero whole-container credit.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Four-card grouping of log and flow terminology. Log Integrity still overstates what hashing establishes without a protected baseline/completeness evidence. Self-rating is not an integrity or monitoring test.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Leadership and data responsibility terms for oversight.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: a leadership/data-responsibility collection needs contextual role distinctions, but its processor body uses third-party language without the required relationship precision and its custodian/steward group supplies technical implementation work only. It does not explain governance/data-quality stewardship or declare a specific combined role. The other five governance/owner/controller definitions do not supply those missing distinctions. This parent needs bounded role context; it is not a new legal applicability determination or automatic transfer of two child holds.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Seven-card grouping of oversight and data-role labels. Data Processor and Data Custodian/Steward remain held; browsing is not a legal role determination or approval of the compound role taxonomy.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Risk scoring, appetite, tolerance, and treatment choices.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the collection includes an unspecified numbered matrix as qualitative and defines tolerance as variation from appetite without an objective/threshold basis. A numeric matrix can encode ordinal categories, semi-quantitative scores or measured quantities; these need different interpretations. Tolerance is not blanket permission to vary outside appetite. The adjacent treatment/register cards do not resolve the scoring and tolerance distinctions that the container explicitly promises.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Nine-card grouping of analysis, appetite, tolerance and treatments. Qualitative Risk Analysis and Risk Tolerance remain held. Formula/label recall does not validate quantitative scoring, risk acceptance or treatment effectiveness.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Cloud models, device security, endpoint management, and industrial systems.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: only16 of32 children are selected; the other16 remain unreviewed, and two selected compound cards are held. Zero whole-container credit.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Thirty-two-card mixed vocabulary collection. All 32 now have prior dispositions: 26 qualified and 6 held. The old premise that only 16 were reviewed is historical; the six compound/ambiguous identity holds remain, so whole-deck teaching is not qualified.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Cloud escape, mobile bypass, firmware persistence, and supply-chain attacks.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the mobile-installation body makes untrusted sourcing intrinsic to off-store installation. A legitimate enterprise/developer installation disproves that equivalence; its adware example illustrates one malicious case without narrowing the definition. The collection otherwise gives VM escape, privilege bypass, firmware, supply-chain and physical examples, but example recall and self-ratings cannot validate compromise. This actual attack-container classification gap prevents whole-container qualification independently of the carried Side-Loading hold.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Six-card collection with authored examples. Side-Loading retains its classification hold; a malicious example does not make every off-store installation malicious, and example recall is not attack-handling skill.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Risk calculations, continuity planning, legal documents, and compliance terms.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the collection promises risk/compliance vocabulary but PHI supplies identifiability without covered-entity/business-associate context or exclusions, and MOA/MOU supplies only a common purpose without contextual distinction. CTF/ISP/OID definitions also supply no explicit bridge to their inherited governance/privacy placement. Clear SLE/ALE/RTO/RPO/MTTR and other introductory definitions do not repair those container content/relevance gaps. No universal MOA-versus-MOU legal rule is invented and no individual/contract/health record is classified.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Thirty-two-card mixed collection spanning risk, continuity, privacy, organizations and identifiers. CTF, ISP, MOA/MOU, OID and PHI remain held; clear recovery/formula cards cannot supply missing context or qualify the whole collection.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Incident response, monitoring centers, and response automation.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: all18 children were inspected, but CIO/CSO teaching and SOC support identity remain held; zero whole-container credit.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Eighteen-card mixed operations collection. CIO/CSO component teaching and SOC support identity remain held; center/chip identity is not resolved by selecting a card or opening a related lesson.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Human-targeted tricks, impersonation, physical observation, and phishing.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the tailgating body classifies following without credentials rather than unauthorized entry, so an authorized escorted visitor is a counterexample to its promised attack classification. The broad-versus-targeted phishing phrasing also remains unclear in an introductory collection containing spear phishing/whaling. A malicious example cannot repair a universal definition or establish exclusive categories. This is a parent content judgment, not automatic inheritance of the existing two child holds.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Thirteen-card collection with authored examples. Phishing and Tailgating retain their exact holds; an authorized escorted visitor defeats credential-only attack classification. Examples do not make attack categories exclusive.

rowDispositions.descriptionObserved: Terms used for detection, threat sharing, email defense, and protective gateways.
rowDispositions.priorReason: HOLD: the collection teaches an unqualified TAXII expansion using historical Indicator wording without a version boundary, and DKIM wording does not separate signing-domain responsibility from the purported author. That weakens its promised CTI/email vocabulary even though the other nine definitions introduce relevant tools. TAXII 2.1 and DKIM primary sources support the version/signer distinctions. No feed, signed message, detection effectiveness, protocol configuration or repaired child credit is inferred.
rowDispositions.currentReview: Eleven-card mixed detection, CTI and email-tool collection. DKIM and TAXII retain their signer/version holds; navigation does not verify an email signature, feed version, gateway policy or detection result.
